verdicts.claim: City Edition history: 2019-20 MECCA floor design and 2018-19 cream look
verdicts.note: Swapped in the dossier. Press coverage shows 2018-19 was the MECCA-floor look and 2019-20 was Cream City. It also turned up 2021-22 franchise history, 2024-25 Wisconsin-outline look and a 2025-26 Cream City return. Rewrote extra.cityEditions.

verdicts.claim: Justin Carlisle's Ardent is a current fine-dining anchor
verdicts.note: Ardent closed Dec 31, 2024, and the space became Purslane (Mary Kastman). Replaced the person entry and the verify line.

verdicts.claim: Mitchell Park Domes are a beloved icon (implied visitable)
verdicts.note: The Domes are still closed for repairs, with renovation groundbreaking targeted for 2027. Kept them as a graphic icon only and updated the culture and underground text.

verdicts.claim: UW-Milwaukee Klotsche Center is the Panthers' basketball home
verdicts.note: Panthers men play at UWM Panther Arena (the Mecca). Klotsche Center hosts women's basketball. Replaced the place.

verdicts.claim: This Is It! is in Walker's Point
verdicts.note: The bar is on E Wells St downtown, just north of the Walker's Point corridor. Fixed the neighborhood. Triangle Bar is the Walker's Point anchor.

verdicts.claim: 'The Land (Good Land)' as a Bucks fan nickname
verdicts.note: 'The Land' is Cleveland's nickname, and no Bucks usage is known. Replaced it with 'Bucks in Six'.

verdicts.claim: 1990s Bucks look described as purple-and-teal (fanbase)
verdicts.note: The 1993-2006 set was purple, green and silver, as the uniform dossier says. Changed fanbase to purple-and-green throughout.

verdicts.claim: UWM Panther Arena is 'where the franchise won in 1971'
verdicts.note: The 1971 champions' home court was the Milwaukee Arena, the Bucks' home through 1988. The title itself was clinched on the road. Reworded.

verdicts.claim: Fear the Deer originated in the 2019 era
verdicts.note: The phrase dates to the mid-2010s and was revived in 2019-21. Reworded.

verdicts.claim: Moncrief and Johnson teams won Central titles
verdicts.note: Changed to division titles. The 1980s Bucks were in the Midwest division for most of the run.

verdicts.claim: Var Gallery is an active Walker's Point gallery
verdicts.note: Could not confirm it is still operating. Replaced it with Black Cat Alley and cut it from the insight text.

verdicts.claim: Sobelman's Pub & Grill sits in Downtown/Walker's Point
verdicts.note: Recalled as Near West Side (Clybourn St), not Walker's Point. Softened the location. Still needs a live check for the current address.

verdicts.claim: Fish fry peaks 'Feb to early April'
verdicts.note: Easter is Mar 28, 2027, so Lenten Fridays run Feb 12 to Mar 26. Changed. Strategy repeats the early-April error.

verdicts.claim: Ethnic fests rotate 'after Summerfest'; Juneteenth 'in Bronzville'
verdicts.note: Polish Fest falls before Summerfest. Fixed the typo and placed Juneteenth generally on the North Side.

verdicts.claim: Cup East Group A 'home Fridays' against all four opponents
verdicts.note: Each team plays each group rival once, so that is two home and two road games. Group play also includes extra Cup Nights on Nov 24-25. Reworded.

verdicts.claim: Harley-Davidson Museum source URL
verdicts.note: Replaced with the museum's own domain, h-dmuseum.com.

verdicts.claim: Deer District Wikipedia source URL
verdicts.note: No standalone article is certain, so the source now points to the Fiserv Forum article.

verdicts.claim: Wisconsin State Fair 'early August'
verdicts.note: The fair typically opens in the last days of July and runs into mid August. Widened the timing across the dossiers.

verdicts.claim: 1971 title look was 'green-and-cream' (fanFavorites)
verdicts.note: Not sure cream was on the 1971 uniforms, so reworded to 'green look'. Also cut an unverified 'Deer statue' reference and the 'MECCA/Bradley-era' conflation.

verdicts.claim: uniform.avoid cites past cream-base and Mecca City Editions
verdicts.note: The direction is right: both were used (2018-19 MECCA, 2019-20 and 2025-26 Cream City). But 2025-26 was a Cream City return, so 'Fired Here' should also avoid a brick-and-cream story so close to last season. Note that 2024-25 used a Wisconsin outline.

verdicts.claim: Two Titles theme: '1971 green-red-and-white script era'
verdicts.note: Script lettering belongs to the 1977-93 era. The 1971 team wore the original 1968-77 set. The editor should separate the two.

verdicts.claim: Lenten Fridays 'Feb to early April'
verdicts.note: Lent 2027 ends Mar 26 (Easter is Mar 28). The editor must change fish-fry-cup-fridays.when to Feb 12 to Mar 26.

verdicts.claim: Cup Night 'home Cup Fridays' and 'Games against Detroit, Toronto, Orlando and Brooklyn' as Fridays at Fiserv Forum
verdicts.note: Only two of the four group games are at home, and not all are Fridays (Nov 24-25 are extra Cup Nights). The editor should say 'home Cup games' and pull dates from the schedule.

verdicts.claim: Cream City Cream appears as #EEE1C6 and #E8D9B0 (Many Milwaukees palette)
verdicts.note: The same named color carries two hex values. Use #EEE1C6 and rename the other swatch.

verdicts.note: Checked live 2026-10-10: Nike's Wisconsin store directory lists the Nike Factory Store at Pleasant Prairie Premium Outlets, 11211 120th Ave., Suite 80.

verdicts.claim: Bronzeville Center for the Arts is operating and open to partnership
verdicts.note: Checked live 2026-10-10: The nonprofit is active. It bought the former DNR building on King Drive for a planned museum, but the museum is not built and its construction timeline depends on fundraising. Partnership openness is still unconfirmed.

verdicts.claim: Sherman Phoenix operating
verdicts.note: Checked live 2026-10-10: An August 2026 Wisconsin Watch story reports the marketplace is open at 3536 W. Fond du Lac Ave. with about 16 businesses, down from a peak near 60. It opened in November 2018, not 2019.

summary: The dossiers were mostly sound on long-established Milwaukee history. They also matched the verified 2026 facts on the Giannis trade, Jenkins, the roster and the Cup group. Fixed: the swapped and incomplete City Edition history (checked live). Also fixed the closed Ardent and Mitchell Park Domes, the Panthers' arena, a Cleveland nickname, purple-teal versus purple-green, Lent timing and Cup home-game wording. Strategy still needs fixes on Lent dates, Cup home Fridays, a duplicated cream hex, the 1971 versus script-era mix-up and City Edition avoidance. Most remaining risk sits in small venues, shops, artists and store doors, queued as unverifiable.
